label: sparse copy-phase update unit, late recall, input-token biased (p most)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, from recall_idx >= 2 on (never in the original phase, never at <DEL>, never on the first two copy outputs). It also never fires when the current input is its first occurrence in the sequence (in_first=0 covers all activations), which is automatic for copy-phase inputs. Within the copy phase it is sparse (about 2.4% of copy steps) and spread over many (L, recall_idx) cells. The highest-rate cells are L=3 recall 2 (24%), L=9 recall 3 (11%) and the final step of L=9 (8.6%). It prefers certain input tokens: p at 8x lift carries 31% of the mass, then r, f, z, j, 2, i, h. Even so, at most 26% of copy-phase p inputs fire. No combination of position, token or history variables reached precision above ~0.26. The recorded predicate (copy phase, recall>=2, input in {p,r,f,z,j,2,i,h}) covers 83% of the mass but has only 9% precision. What makes it fire seems to depend on sequence content that these variables do not capture. The strongest activations are on input p (or r) at the last or second-to-last copy step of L=9 sequences.
